text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- People's Action Party is likely to be returned to power when nominations close for country's eight General Election since independence.
- People's Action Party will fight general election as 'local government election' pitting its ward programmes against what opposition has to offer.
- Peru President Alberto Fujimori tells rebels to give up fight and he will not use force against them if they surrender their arms and freed all captives.
- Funds raised through initial public offerings this year is about Singapore $800 million.
- China will accelerate listings of new firms on its two stock markets next year to meet demand and curb speculation.
- Thai exporters urge government to boost competitiveness.
- Private pension schemes by local companies are likely to take off in big way over next few years.
- Top foreign building firms are pulling out of Taiwan due to delays in implementing a US$308 billion government infrastructure programme.
- Apple Computer Inc's decision to bring back Steve Jobs is expected to return company to forefront of personal computer industry.

- Shanghai International-APS, a fund management joint venture wbetween China's biggest broker and a Singaporean, plans to expand business in Singapore with funds of Singapore $250 million by next year.
- Ossia International wins three new distributorships expected to boost its sales and profits.
